newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GPT says well placed for purchases.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GPT says well placed for purchases.

text.p: GPT Management Ltd, manager of General Property Trust (GPT), said on Thursday that GPT could spend up to A$300 million on acquisitions without raising extra capital or selling assets.

GPT Management chief executive David Ross said GPT had about 11 percent of its assets in borrowings which could comfortably go to 25 percent without further borrowings. He said the trust had about A$150 million committed to capital expenditure.
Ross said GPT also had funds available from a commercial paper programme. "Put all that together and we would somewhere in the order of A$300 million," Ross told reporters.
GPT earlier reported a 36.7 percent rise in net profit to A$167.72 million in calendar 1996.
Ross said GPT was interested in increasing its exposure in the office sector and was also interested in entering the hotel sector, but there were no specfic acquisition plans.
"One area we would like to move into that we are not presently in is the hotel sector, but it is very early days," Ross told reporters after the GPT results announcement.
Ross said the group would also consider offers for some of its assets if the right price came along. In 1996, GPT acquired the GEM property trusts for A$900 million.
At 11.40 p.m. (0040 GMT), GPT units were two cents up at A$2.43.
